items.title: New tools: ID converter, bulk downloads, synteny & variation
items.body: Four additions for working with the data. A gene ID converter maps a mixed list of symbols, DDB_G, UniProt, and NCBI ids into one table. Whole-database TSV downloads (genes, GO, phenotypes, human orthologs) are now on the downloads page. And every gene record's Orthologs tab gains a genomic-neighborhood view that checks whether local gene order is conserved across the dictyostelids, plus a natural-variation panel comparing the protein across the wild D. discoideum isolates.

items.title: New dictyostelid genomes: wild isolates and two more species
items.body: Genome assemblies and annotations from Ahmed et al. 2025 (PNAS) are now on the site. Two new species — D. citrinum and D. dimigraforme — join the comparative tools, and a panel of wild D. discoideum isolates (AX2-214, CR116C, OT3A, M4B, S6B) is now available alongside them. Search any of them with BLAST, view them in the genome browser, or grab the FASTA and annotations on the genome downloads page. Released under CC BY 4.0.

items.title: Annotations now refresh automatically
items.body: Human orthologs, the UniProt accession map, and protein-domain architecture now update each month from UniProt, OMA, and InterPro, so the data stays current without manual rebuilds. Protein domains are precomputed for faster loading on the Structures tab, with a live lookup as a fallback.

items.title: A much faster genome browser
items.body: The genome browser now opens in about a second instead of ten — gene annotations are served from indexed files, so only the region you're viewing is fetched. Same data, far less waiting.

items.title: Command palette, gene basket, and advanced search
items.body: Press ⌘K (or /) to jump to any gene, page, or tool. Collect genes into a basket and send the whole set into enrichment or expression tools. And filter the catalog by phenotype, human ortholog, disease link, or expression peak in the new advanced finder.

items.title: Lab tools: CRISPR guides, qPCR primers, and codon optimization
items.body: Design SpCas9 guides for a gene (with genome off-target checking), qPCR primers over its cDNA, and codon-optimize a sequence for Dictyostelium's AT-rich codon usage. Under Useful tools → Lab tools.

items.title: Compare expression and find co-expressed genes
items.body: Overlay the developmental RNA-seq profiles of several genes, and see the most co-expressed genes right on each gene record. RNA-seq is also now an overlay track in the genome browser.

items.title: Human disease models
items.body: Gene records now show human orthologs and their disease associations, plus a browsable Dictyostelium disease-models page — a starting point for using the amoeba as a model system.

items.title: AI-suggested annotations (clearly badged)
items.body: A third, machine-generated curation layer offers AI summaries and GO suggestions for many genes. It is unreviewed and always badged ‘AI’ — a starting point, never a substitute for curated evidence.

items.title: Welcome to Dicty@Duke (beta)
items.body: A modern interface over Dictyostelid genomes and curation: searchable gene records with structures and expression, a genome browser, BLAST, GO/phenotype enrichment, and a public REST API. Feedback and corrections welcome.
